title: Ragi Mudde
description: Finger-millet flour cooked and kneaded into a smooth, dense ball — a Karnataka staple, eaten by breaking off small pieces and dipping into a curry.
steps: Bring two-thirds of the water to a boil in a heavy-bottomed pot with the salt.
Mix the ragi flour with the remaining cold water to form a smooth, lump-free slurry.
Reduce the boiling water to a simmer and pour in the ragi slurry, stirring continuously to prevent lumps.
Cook, stirring constantly, for 8-10 minutes until the mixture thickens into a dense, glossy mass that pulls away from the sides of the pot.
Wet a wooden spoon or your hands (curd or water helps prevent sticking) and quickly shape the hot mixture into smooth, round balls while it's still warm.
Serve hot, breaking off small pieces to dip into sambar or a spicy curry.
